arms.predicted: NN construction + spatial NN-list 2-opt (K=20) + window 2-opt + carrot will score significantly higher than iter-1's 55.4 baseline, achieving approximately 70-80 on the judge.
arms.observed: SCORE: 76.319 (3 runs, all identical). The algorithm scores 76.319 consistently — well within the predicted 70-80 range. This represents a 20.9 point improvement over iter-1's 55.4 baseline. The perfect reproducibility (0 variance across 3 runs) indicates the NN 2-opt converges before the time limit when starting from an NN-constructed tour.
arms.diagnostic_note: Score reproducibility (std=0.0) is a bonus finding: NN construction produces a tour close enough to the 2-opt local optimum that convergence is time-insensitive within the 2.5s budget. This makes the algorithm deployable without tuning.

arms.predicted: Strip construction + spatial NN-list 2-opt (same K=20 and optimization phases as h-main) will score higher than iter-1's 55.4 but lower than h-main, in the range 65-75.
arms.observed: SCORES: 61.316, 66.729, 70.634, 66.109 (4 runs, mean=66.197, std=3.82). The mean score (66.2) is within the predicted 65-75 range but individual runs span 61.3 to 70.6. The high variance (std=3.82 vs h-main's std=0.0) reveals that strip construction produces a worse initial tour that the time-budgeted NN 2-opt cannot fully optimize before the limit on large test cases. The directional prediction holds: h-ablation (mean 66.2) > iter-1 baseline (55.4) < h-main (76.3).
arms.diagnostic_note: The ~10 point gap between h-main (76.3) and h-ablation mean (66.2) is larger than the predicted ~5 points (from proto_v4's 71.2 vs proto_v5's 76.0). The discrepancy comes from two sources: (1) proto_v4 had K=10 which may have been closer to optimal for strip construction (less precompute time, more 2-opt time), and (2) the high variance means some runs (70.6) match the prediction while others (61.3) dramatically underperform. The construction heuristic contributes both quality (better initial tour) and stability (more deterministic convergence).

discrepancy_analysis: Both arm predictions confirmed directionally. h-main scored 76.319 (predicted 70-80, confirmed). h-ablation scored mean 66.2 (predicted 65-75, confirmed on average). The main unexpected finding is the dramatic variance difference: h-main has 0 variance while h-ablation has std=3.82. This reveals that NN construction's value is not just a better initial tour but also convergence stability — the NN-constructed tour is close enough to the 2-opt local optimum that time budget doesn't matter, while strip construction leaves the optimizer still improving when time runs out on large test cases. The gap between h-main and h-ablation (10.1 points) is larger than the designer predicted (~5 points from proto comparisons), because proto_v4 used K=10 while our ablation uses K=20 — the larger K increases precompute time without proportional benefit for strip construction's worse starting point.
